concepts.name: Probability Fundamentals
concepts.description: Core rules of sample spaces, mutually exclusive events, and basic probability axioms.
concepts.summaryNotes: P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersect B). Total probability over sample space S equals 1.

concepts.name: Random Variables
concepts.description: Discrete vs continuous random variables, probability mass functions, and expectation.
concepts.summaryNotes: A random variable assigns real numbers to outcomes. Expected value E[X] = sum(x * P(X=x)).

concepts.name: Conditional Probability
concepts.description: The probability of event A given event B has already occurred: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).
concepts.summaryNotes: Conditioning reduces the sample space to B. If events are independent, P(A|B) = P(A).

concepts.name: Probability Distributions
concepts.description: Gaussian (Normal), Bernoulli, Binomial, and Poisson probability distributions.
concepts.summaryNotes: Gaussian is parameterized by mean mu and variance sigma^2. Central limit theorem applies.

concepts.name: Bayes Theorem
concepts.description: Formulating posterior beliefs from likelihood and priors: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B).
concepts.summaryNotes: Posterior = (Likelihood * Prior) / Evidence. Crucial when inverting conditional statements.

concepts.name: Naive Bayes
concepts.description: Applying Bayes theorem with conditional independence assumption between every pair of features.
concepts.summaryNotes: Assumes features are conditionally independent given class y. P(x1, x2 | y) = P(x1|y) * P(x2|y).

concepts.name: Classification
concepts.description: Mapping inputs to discrete categories; decision boundaries and multi-class schemes.
concepts.summaryNotes: Predicts categorical target labels using learned decision boundary.

concepts.name: Model Evaluation
concepts.description: Confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC metrics.
concepts.summaryNotes: Precision = TP / (TP + FP). Recall = TP / (TP + FN). F1 balances both harmonic mean.

concepts.name: Hypothesis Testing
concepts.description: Null hypothesis, alternative hypothesis, p-values, and significance level alpha.
concepts.summaryNotes: Reject null hypothesis if p-value < alpha (e.g. 0.05). Type I and Type II errors.

concepts.name: Linear Regression
concepts.description: Modeling relationship between scalar response and one or more explanatory variables.
concepts.summaryNotes: y = beta_0 + beta_1 * x + epsilon. Cost function minimizes sum of squared residuals.

questions.question: What is the probability of getting a head in a fair coin toss?
questions.explanation: A fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes (Head, Tail). The probability of Head is 1/2.

questions.question: If two fair dice are rolled, what is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.explanation: There are 6 winning pairs: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) out of 36 total outcomes: 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.question: Given P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. What is P(A | B)?
Given P(A) = 0.6, P(B|A) = 0.7, and P(B|Aᶜ) = 0.2. Find P(A | B).

A test for a rare disease is 99% accurate (sensitivity = 99%, specificity = 99%). The disease prevalence is 0.1% (1 in 1000). A patient tests positive. What is the approximate probability they actually have the disease?
questions.explanation: Base rate fallacy! Out of 100,000 people, 100 have it (99 test +), while 99,900 are healthy (999 test false +). P(Disease|Positive) = 99 / (99 + 999) ≈ 9%.

questions.question: What is the foundational assumption that gives Naive Bayes its name?
options: Features are conditionally independent given the class label
Features are normally distributed with zero mean
Classes are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
The loss function is strictly convex
questions.correctAnswer: Features are conditionally independent given the class label
questions.explanation: Naive Bayes assumes that all feature predictors are conditionally independent given the target class label.

questions.question: Which metric is best when dealing with high class imbalance where false negatives are very costly (e.g. cancer detection)?
questions.explanation: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). When false negatives must be minimized at all costs, recall is paramount.

What mathematical function describes the probability distribution of a continuous random variable?
questions.explanation: Continuous random variables are defined by a Probability Density Function (PDF), where probabilities correspond to integrals over intervals.

questions.question: In hypothesis testing, what does a p-value of 0.03 mean if your significance level α = 0.05?
options: Reject the null hypothesis because p ≤ α
Fail to reject the null hypothesis because p > α
The probability that H₀ is true is 3%
The experiment failed due to insufficient data
questions.correctAnswer: Reject the null hypothesis because p ≤ α
questions.explanation: Since p (0.03) is less than α (0.05), the observed data is statistically significant evidence against the null hypothesis H₀.

questions.question: According to the Central Limit Theorem, what happens to the sampling distribution of the sample mean as sample size n increases?
options: Becomes heavily skewed to the right
questions.explanation: The Central Limit Theorem proves that sample means approach a Normal distribution for large sample sizes (n ≥ 30).

questions.question: In Pandas, which method is used to filter rows based on boolean conditional logic?
questions.explanation: Boolean indexing in Pandas passes a conditional expression inside square brackets to select rows.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: Balanced BSTs halve the search space at each comparison step, yielding logarithmic O(log n) time complexity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Coffman’s four necessary conditions for OS deadlock?
